newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK protesters gather outside Japanese consuluate.
newsitem.headline: HK protesters gather outside Japanese consuluate.

text.p: Protesters gathered outside the Japanese Consulate in Hong Kong on Friday to mark the 59th anniversary of the Nanking Massacre, demanding Tokyo apologise for war-time atrocities
Waving banners reading "Japanese atrocities cannot be forgiven" and "Down with Japanese militarism", about 30 protesters also sought reparations for victims of Japanese aggression.
The group delivered a petition to consulate staff.
In 1937, thousands were killed by the Japanese Army at the Nationalist Chinese capital of Nanking, renamed Nanjing when the communists took power in China after the war.

A wave of anti-Japanese protests swept Hong Kong in August and September after Japanese extremists erected a light house and war memorial on disputed islands in the East China Sea that are also claimed by China.
The sentiment reached its height when a protest leader drowned off the isles and protesters planted a Communist Chinese and Taiwan Nationalist flag on the isles in early October.
